entries.appliesTo: persons who distribute nonconsensual synthetic sexual material, develop or distribute AI systems designed for child pornography or self-harm promotion, or use AI to generate or possess AI-generated child pornography

dutySources.statutory-review: AN ACT — 'relating to crimes and offenses; specifying that using artificial intelligence to commit a criminal offense shall not be a defense to the offense; establishing criminal offenses concerning the use of synthetic sexual material or artificial intelligence against children'

sources.prohibition: § 6-4-307(a)(i)(A) — 'Knowingly, distributes, transmits or otherwise makes available synthetic sexual material that realistically depicts another identifiable person without that person's knowledge or consent'
sources.penaltyMax: § 6-4-307(c)(i) — 'a felony punishable by imprisonment for not more than ten (10) years, a fine of not more than ten thousand dollars ($10,000.00), or both'
sources.penaltyUnit: § 6-4-307(c)(ii) — 'For a second or subsequent conviction under this section or of a substantially similar law of any other jurisdiction, a felony punishable by imprisonment for not more than twelve (12) years, a fine of not more than ten thousand dollars ($10,000.00), or both'
sources.enforcer: § 6-1-206(a) — 'Nothing in the Wyoming Criminal Code shall be construed to prohibit the application of this code against activity facilitated by an artificial intelligence system'

flags: prohibition param is lossy: bill also criminalizes csam (§ 6-4-308 — 'Knowingly develops or distributes an artificial intelligence system specifically designed to create, distribute or promote child pornography'; § 6-4-303(b)(v) — 'Uses an artificial intelligence system to generate or create child pornography'; (b)(vi) — 'Possesses child pornography that the person knows was generated by an artificial intelligence system') and suicide-encouragement (§ 6-4-701 — 'artificial intelligence system specifically designed to promote self-harm')
coveredSubjects param is lossy: NCII offense (§ 6-4-307) covers all identifiable persons; the CSAM offenses (§§ 6-4-308, 6-4-303) cover minors

imprisonment tiers: all new offenses are felonies up to 10 years (§ 6-4-307(c)(i), § 6-4-308(d), § 6-4-701(d)); 12 years for second/subsequent NCII conviction (§ 6-4-307(c)(ii)); amended § 6-4-303(c) sets 5–12 years for AI-generated child pornography creation, § 6-4-303(d) up to 10 years for possession, § 6-4-303(e) 7–12 years for repeat convictions — every fine is capped at $10,000
sextortion prong: § 6-4-307(a)(iii) criminalizes threats to distribute synthetic sexual material 'to obtain a benefit'

developer civil immunity (not a duty): § 1-1-143(b) — 'the developer of an artificial intelligence system shall not be liable for damages arising from the use of an artificial intelligence system when another person used the system with the intent to commit or engage in illegal or illicit activities or to cause harm', lost if 'developed with the knowledge or intent that the primary purpose of the system would be for illegal or illicit activities' (§ 1-1-143(c))
no-AI-defense rule: § 6-1-206(b) — 'The use of an artificial intelligence system by a person to commit a criminal offense shall not be a defense to a criminal charge'
title/text mismatch: the AN ACT clause references offenses for using AI 'to censor political speech', but the enacted text creates no such offense (Article 7 contains only § 6-4-701 self-harm)
Section 230 carve-outs: §§ 6-4-307(d), 6-4-308(c)(iv), 6-4-701(c)(v) exempt interactive computer services and information/telecommunications services 'for content provided by another person'
user-prompt safe harbor for developers: §§ 6-4-308(c)(i), 6-4-701(c)(i) exempt systems producing prohibited content 'solely as a result of user prompts or inputs' without developer intent
title mentions 'providing causes of action' but the only civil provision in the text is the § 1-1-143 immunity; no new cause of action is expressly created
